claims.text: Single-phase solid-solution crystal-structure selection in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by competition between atomic diffusion and nucleation.
A moderate thermal ramp provides sufficient atomic mobility for interdiffusion to balance nucleation and preserve a single-phase structure.
Ultra-rapid temperature changes freeze in elemental segregation and phase separation.
Rapid heating and cooling frequently produce phase separation in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Rapid heating and cooling frequently produce elemental segregation in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Rapid heating and cooling frequently produce uncontrolled nanoparticle morphologies.
The thermal ramp rate should be varied while composition, nanoparticle size, and other processing parameters are held constant.
The proposed regime applies to nanoparticles containing more than five noble-metal elements.
Homogeneous mixing is possible only within a suitable window of mixing enthalpy and atomic-size differences.
Transient thermal processing controls the effective atomic diffusion length.
Transient thermal processing controls the density of nucleation sites.
Atomic diffusion length and nucleation-site density govern the degree of elemental intermixing.
Under ultra-rapid thermal ramps, limited atomic mobility causes premature nucleation.
Premature nucleation under ultra-rapid ramps freezes compositional heterogeneities.
A moderated ramp permits diffusion and elemental intermixing before the phase transition is completed.
Greater intermixing before completion of the phase transition promotes a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
A moderated thermal ramp will reduce elemental segregation relative to the ultra-rapid baseline.
A moderated thermal ramp will reduce phase impurities relative to the ultra-rapid baseline.
A moderated thermal ramp will improve crystal-structure uniformity relative to the ultra-rapid baseline.
Outside the suitable mixing-enthalpy and atomic-radius window, thermal-ramp control may be insufficient to form a homogeneous single phase.
